claims.text: Phase stability in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni high-entropy alloys is governed by the degree of local atomic ordering.
Local atomic ordering is driven by inter-element d-electron interactions.
Increasing Al concentration within a moderate range increases the ordering enthalpy.
When ordering enthalpy exceeds the destabilizing effect of configurational entropy, a nanoscale B2-like ordered phase forms within a disordered matrix.
Interfaces associated with the nanoscale ordered phase mechanically reinforce the alloy.
Interfaces associated with the nanoscale ordered phase act as defect sinks.
An equiatomic or low-Al near-equiatomic Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni alloy is predominantly disordered and single phase.
Increasing Al content and applying controlled heat treatments promotes local atomic ordering.
B2-like ordered clusters impede dislocation motion and thereby enhance high-temperature strength.
Stable ordered/disordered interfaces arrest radiation-induced defects and improve radiation tolerance.
B2-like ordered clusters hinder crack propagation and improve low-temperature toughness.
The proposed ordering can improve mechanical and radiation-related properties without sacrificing environmental durability.
An optimal moderate Al level will produce detectable nanoscale B2-like ordering.
The optimally ordered alloy will have higher high-temperature strength than a lower-Al disordered baseline.
The optimally ordered alloy will have better radiation tolerance than a lower-Al disordered baseline.
The optimally ordered alloy will have better environmental resistance than a lower-Al disordered baseline.
The optimally ordered alloy will maintain cryogenic toughness relative to a lower-Al disordered baseline.
An Al range of approximately 10–20 at.% is sufficient to induce nanoscale ordering without causing bulk phase segregation or embrittlement.
Extreme compositional deviations or significant processing changes may produce different phase behavior.
Failure of increased Al to increase ordering, or failure of ordering to improve performance relative to the disordered baseline, is designated as falsifying the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The initial state permits an equiatomic alloy, which has 20 at.% Al, while the intervention calls for increasing Al within a stated 10–20 at.% range. Starting from the equiatomic option leaves no room to increase Al while remaining within that boundary.

The mechanism says ordering improves low-temperature toughness, whereas the predicted outcome only requires that cryogenic toughness be maintained. These are different outcome strengths, although not strictly mutually exclusive.
